drafted_from: tool:judge-one-shot-sounds-as-whole-sounds row in tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/tool-rows.json, its script in tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/do-work/ and tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/test/test_judge_sound_effects.py (run for real on made-up tones)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Judge /work/sfx/hits/b.wav as a whole sound against the description a high blip, with a door and a knock as alternatives." It runs the whole-sound listener and reads back the trim and the match.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads sound files named on the command line and merges its readings into an OUT.json file on this computer.
instructions: 1. Pick the one-shot sound files, for example /work/sfx/hits/b.wav, and the description to judge them against ("a high blip"); optionally alternatives separated by | ("a door|a knock").

2. Say "Judge these as whole sounds". The AI reads the row with tools:list and runs: EARSHOT_THREADS=3 <earshot python> -I tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/do-work/listen_to_whole_sounds.py /work/sfx/whole.json "a high blip" "a door|a knock" /work/sfx/hits/b.wav
3. Read the last line (how many files were heard), then open whole.json: each entry is keyed "<file>::<query>" and holds the trim, head_db, tail_db, match z, realness, describe and measures.

worked_examples.title: A 2000 Hz blip judged whole from its first onset to its tail
worked_examples.ask: Judge this blip as a whole sound for "a high blip".

Command: EARSHOT_THREADS=3 python -I tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/do-work/listen_to_whole_sounds.py /work/sfx/whole.json "a high blip" "a door|a knock" /work/sfx/hits/b.wav
